descriptionChirho: To stand near, beside, or among others, indicating physical presence or proximity as a bystander or onlooker (Mark 14:47,69-70, 15:35,39, Luke 1:19, 19:24, John 18:22, 19:26, Acts 1:10, 4:10,26, 9:39, 23:2,4, 27:23).

To present, offer, or yield someone or something formally before another, whether in a religious, legal, or moral context, including presenting oneself or one's body (Luke 2:22, Acts 1:3, 9:41, 23:33, Rom 6:13,16,19, 12:1, 1 Cor 8:8, 2 Cor 4:14, 11:2, Eph 5:27, Col 1:22,28, 2 Tim 2:15).
To stand alongside someone in a supportive capacity, providing help or assistance in a time of need (Rom 16:2, 2 Tim 4:17).
To provide, furnish, or make available something for use, such as troops or resources (Matt 26:53, Acts 23:24).
To stand before a judge, tribunal, or divine authority, implying a judicial or eschatological appearance (Acts 27:24, Rom 14:10).
To prove or demonstrate something, to establish the truth of a claim (Acts 24:13).
To be present in the sense of having come or arrived; used of a time or season that has drawn near (Mark 4:29, of the harvest being at hand).
